question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [English interactions with local Mughal subahdars and governors]
options: Shaista Khan — Bengal (governor who clashed with the English, leading to the sack of Hooghly in 1686)
Muqarrab Khan — Surat (Mughal official who initially obstructed English trade to appease the Portuguese)
Mir Jumla — Bengal (Mughal governor who regulated English saltpetre trade and restricted their privileges)
Asaf Khan — Masulipatnam (Mughal subahdar who leased the port to Hawkins for establishing a factory)
wrong_fact: Asaf Khan was the brother of Nur Jahan and a high-ranking minister/wazir at the Mughal central court in Agra, not a local subahdar of Masulipatnam. Furthermore, Masulipatnam was under the Golconda Sultanate, not the Mughal Empire, in the early 17th century.
explanation: Shaista Khan was the Subahdar of Bengal who clashed with the English (1686). Muqarrab Khan was the custom officer/governor of Surat who resisted the English to maintain Portuguese trade. Mir Jumla was the governor of Bengal who tightly regulated EIC trade. Asaf Khan was an influential minister at the Agra court, and Masulipatnam was part of the Golconda kingdom, not Mughal territory during Hawkins's or Roe's visits.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Mughal officers, regions of conflict, and English actions]
options: Shaista Khan — Bengal (expelled the English from Hooghly in 1686 after EIC forces raided Mughal posts)
Muqarrab Khan — Surat (refused English settlement rights until Thomas Best's victory over the Portuguese in 1612)
Shayista Khan — Deccan (agreed to transfer Bombay to the English in 1662 to combat Shivaji's forces)
Saadat Khan — Agra (supervised EIC operations in upper India and collected imperial toll dues)
wrong_fact: Bombay was not transferred to the English by the Mughal governor Shaista Khan. It was ceded by Portugal directly to King Charles II of England in 1661 as part of a marriage treaty/dowry, and later leased to the East India Company.
explanation: Shaista Khan was the Mughal governor of Bengal who drove the English out of Hooghly in 1686. Muqarrab Khan was the governor of Surat who was influenced by the Portuguese. Saadat Khan was a later Mughal administrator in northern India, but Bombay's transfer was a European treaty (between England and Portugal in 1661), completely independent of Shaista Khan or any Mughal provincial authority in the Deccan.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Geographical locations and the specific Mughal officials who governed EIC trade there]
options: Surat — Muqarrab Khan (resisted Hawkins's trade requests; later pacified by EIC naval victories)
Dhaka (Bengal) — Shaista Khan (subahdar who levied 3.5% Jizya/tribute on EIC trade, sparking hostilities)
Agra — Asaf Khan (wazir who acted as Sir Thomas Roe's primary contact and channel to Emperor Jahangir)
Madras — Mir Jumla (Mughal subahdar of Deccan who granted the English the Golden Farman in 1632)
wrong_fact: The 'Golden Farman' of 1632 was granted by the Sultan of Golconda (Abdullah Qutb Shah), not by Mir Jumla or a Mughal subahdar. In 1632, Madras and Golconda were not part of the Mughal Empire.
explanation: Muqarrab Khan (Surat), Shaista Khan (Dhaka/Bengal), and Asaf Khan (Agra) are accurately matched. The Golden Farman of 1632, which allowed the English to trade freely in Golconda ports for a fixed payment, was issued by the Sultan of Golconda, not by the Mughals, who had not yet annexed the Deccan kingdoms.
